notes: Parts are the same as step 1. Only the labels of pot1 and pot2 changed: in the image the upper pot's blue wire goes to A1 and the lower pot's goes to A0. Both pots are still wired to A0 and A1 as the manual says.

Matrix pins follow the manual's table, and each pin number is mapped to the catalogue port that the card assigns to that pin. Pin 1=R5, 2=R7, 3=C2, 4=C3, 5=R8, 6=C5, 7=R6, 8=R3, 9=R1, 10=C4, 11=C6, 12=R4, 13=C1, 14=R2, 15=C7, 16=C8.

Arduino pin to matrix pin follows the table too. 2 to 9, 3 to 10, 4 to 11, 5 to 12, 6 to 13, 7 to 14, 8 to 15, 9 to 16, 10 to 4, 11 to 3, 12 to 2, 13 to 1, A2 (16) to 5, A3 (17) to 6, A4 (18) to 7, A5 (19) to 8.

As in the image, the 1k resistors sit on the yellow wires from Arduino pins 2-9 to matrix pins 9-16. Those pins are a mix of rows and columns. The 8 green wires from pins 10-13 and A2-A5 go straight to matrix pins 1-8 with no resistor.
Each yellow run is modelled as Arduino pin, then a yellow wire, then the resistor, then a second yellow wire, then the matrix. The resistor leads are twisted to the wire ends.

The breadboard hole positions are approximate readings of the image, which numbers rows 1-30 down the board and lettered columns across it. In the catalogue naming that gives '<row number><t or b>.<letter>'. The right-hand power rail is named tp (+) and tn (-). The pots hold no other parts. Each pot has its wiper (SIG) in a column on the a-e side and its two outer terminals in two columns on the f-j side. The black wire goes from the GND terminal to the - rail and the red wire from VCC to the + rail.
The breadboard + rail is fed from 5V and the - rail from the first GND pin (GND.1).
